newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares reap gains from excess liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares reap gains from excess liquidity.

text.p: Surplus money flowing into Nigerian stocks pushed up prices on Monday, further heightening interest in the share market, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at a new record of 7951.19 against 7909.39 on Friday.
Traders said the capital market was awash with funds coming from the banking system where interest rates have fallen.

"More funds are still coming in this week as the finance ministry releases some 44 billion naira capital budget money, in addition to 29 billion from the special petroleum trust fund already in bank vaults," one said.
Banks, foods, conglomerates, industrial/domestic products and petroleum marketers saw increased business.
Buyers took a break from PZ Industries shares on Monday as the stock closed unchanged at 23.80 naira.
But Lever Brothers rose 20 kobo to 22.00 naira and UAC was up 10 kobo to 11.80 naira.
Cadbury advanced 20 kobo to 34.60 naira, Nigerian Bottling Company rose 40 kobo to 46.50 naira while Nestle closed 10 kobo up at 63.40 naira.
Shares of banks kept moving up as investors profited from the government's order that banks raise their capital base nine-fold to 500 million naira by end-1998.
Afribank at 6.65 naira, First Bank at 15.35 naira and NAL Merchant Bank at 5.05 naira were all 15 kobo gainers.
Oil marketer Total went 20 kobo higher at 71.70 naira, African Petroleum, 30 kobo up at 57.00 naira and Agip, up 10 kobo at 29.70 naira.
Vitafoam, Alumaco were impressive, both finishing 10 kobo higher at 4.56 naira and 3.55 naira respectively. Industrial Gas rose 20 kobo to 15.20 naira.
Also benefiting from growing interest in shares was footwear firm Bata, up three kobo, the maximum five percent allowed daily, at 81 kobo.

Trading saw only four losers, led by stationery firm WTN, down five kobo at 6.70 naira. Livestock Feeds, Jos International Breweries and Amicable Assurance ended at 4.61 naira, 40 kobo and 65 kobo, respectively.
